raw_response:
I only have 2.6 mu, so every bag of input matters. I do not make big changes unless I see it work nearby. Last year, if cotton stood well and gave me a fair harvest, I will stay close to that way and only tighten it a little. Around our place, if neighbors use a better cotton seed and it comes up evenly, I will use improved seed too. On fertilizer, I would rather spend a bit more than let the cotton run short, because once yield drops, that loss is bigger than wasting some fertilizer. I have well water, so I am not as scared of dry spells, and I will plan a few irrigations at key times instead of waiting too long. My land is small, so family labor can handle most work. I will plough before sowing, put most phosphorus and potassium in the base, split nitrogen into base plus topdressing, spray several times for aphids, bollworm, and later pests if they show up, and aim for a steady harvest instead of gambling on cutting cost too hard.
